title.rendered: Jehovah Rapha, the Lord Who Heals: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: At the bitter waters of Marah, God did not just sweeten the water. He revealed a name: Jehovah Rapha, the Lord who heals.

content.rendered:
At the bitter waters of Marah, God did not just sweeten the water. He revealed a name: Jehovah Rapha, the Lord who heals.

The Gospel For Today | Thursday, August 13, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“and said, ‘If you diligently heed the voice of the LORD your God and do what is right in His sight, give ear to His commandments and keep all His statutes, I will put none of the diseases on you which I have brought on the Egyptians. For I am the LORD who heals you.’”
Exodus 15:26 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Israel had just crossed the Red Sea. They had watched Pharaoh’s army swallowed by water that had, moments earlier, stood like a wall on their behalf. And three days later, at a place called Marah, they hit water they could not drink — bitter, undrinkable, a small disappointment after a great miracle. It is often in the small disappointments after the great deliverance that a believer discovers a new name of God.

Moses cried out, and the Lord showed him a tree. He threw it into the waters, and the waters were made sweet (Exodus 15:25). Immediately after, before any illness had even appeared among them, God introduced Himself by a new name: Jehovah Rapha, the Lord who heals. Not the Lord who will heal if you get sick. The Lord who heals, present tense, already established as part of who He is before the need arose.

The New Living Translation renders the promise plainly: “I am the Lord who heals you.” (Exodus 15:26 NLT). The Hebrew rapha covers more than physical sickness — it is used throughout scripture for mending what is broken, restoring what is bitter, repairing what has been damaged, whether in the body, the mind, or a relationship. The bitter water at Marah was not a medical condition. It was simply bitter. And Jehovah Rapha’s healing reached even that.

There is a pattern worth noticing: the tree that sweetened the water was not itself sweet. God used an ordinary, unremarkable branch, applied in obedience, to release supernatural healing into an impossible situation. The New Testament believer sees the shadow clearly — another tree, another act of obedience, through which “by His stripes we are healed” (Isaiah 53:5, 1 Peter 2:24).

Whatever is bitter to you today — a diagnosis, a memory, a relationship that has gone sour, a body that will not cooperate — bring it to Jehovah Rapha. He does not need the water to change first. He changes the water.

Prayer

Father, You are Jehovah Rapha, the Lord who heals. I bring You what is bitter in my life today — in my body, my mind, my relationships. I trust You to do what only You can do: turn bitter into sweet, sickness into wholeness, brokenness into repair. Thank You for the tree that heals every bitter water. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

My God is Jehovah Rapha. He is the Lord who heals me, in body, mind, and spirit. What is bitter in my life today will be made sweet by His hand. By His stripes I am healed.
